pages.title: Nuclear power in space — US lunar fission reactor

facts.text: US plan: Lunar Fission Surface Power Project — small fission reactor on the Moon by early 2030s, for NASA's Artemis Base Camp
facts.head: News

facts.text: ⚠ Would be the first permanent nuclear power source beyond Earth orbit
facts.head: News

facts.text: Technology: RTG (Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator); Key point: Decay heat of plutonium-238; few hundred watts; Voyager, New Horizons, Curiosity, Perseverance
facts.head: Space nuclear technologies

facts.text: Technology: Compact fission reactor; Key point: Shipping-container size; 10–100 kW; NASA KRUSTY demo up to 10 kW
facts.head: Space nuclear technologies

facts.text: Technology: Nuclear Thermal Propulsion (NTP); Key point: Reactor heats propellant (liquid hydrogen); high thrust; US DRACO test by 2026
facts.head: Space nuclear technologies

facts.text: Technology: Nuclear Electric Propulsion (NEP); Key point: Reactor electricity powers ion/plasma thrusters; low continuous thrust
facts.head: Space nuclear technologies

facts.text: Why needed: lunar night about 14 Earth days, below –170°C; Mars dust storms
facts.head: Space nuclear technologies

facts.text: Outer Space Treaty 1967, Article IV: bans nuclear weapons/WMDs in orbit and on celestial bodies — ⚠ does not ban peaceful nuclear power
facts.head: Legal framework

facts.text: UN Principles on Nuclear Power Sources in Outer Space, 1992 (UNGA Res. 47/68): non-binding; ⚠ ignore NTP/NEP propulsion
facts.head: Legal framework

facts.text: 1972 Liability Convention: absolute liability for damage on Earth/aircraft; fault-based in outer space
facts.head: Legal framework

facts.text: COPUOS: UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space
facts.head: Legal framework
